HealthSignalKind.description:
What a signal noticed. Only what Agentry can tell from what it already receives is here: a command that runs far longer than it should, a chat that has gone quiet while it should be working, and facts of the chat itself (how its last execution ended, that it waits for a person, that its context is nearly full, that a branch failed).

The second group comes from docs/plans/agent-observability.md and is about a worker that is busy without getting anywhere: the same tool call over and over (`repeat-stall`), no commit and no file touched for a long stretch (`no-progress`), the same few steps in a cycle (`loop`), a test edited so that it stops asserting what it asserted (`weakened-test`), and the ceiling of  {@link  TaskLimits }  coming close (`budget`).

Where a provider stands on this host. Detection returns one of these, never a raw error, so the UI can offer the one remedy that fits:

- `signed-out`: installed and compatible, no credentials.

- `not-installed`: no trace of it.

responsibility.description: One line on what it answers for

ProjectTeamRole.description: A role of the project's team as a template or the settings describe it. `role` is free text (`product-owner`, `developer`, `qa`…) until the Team module defines its roles.

id.description: Ours and stable: the key changes with the prefix, the id never does

description.description: Markdown. Left out of board and list payloads (the board, the lists and their pages, a chat's items), where it is `''` and  {@link  WorkItem.hasDescription }  says whether there is one: the item's own page fetches it (`GET /work-items/:itemId`, `GET /work-items/by-key/:key`).

worktree.description: The item's own git worktree, once something worked on it, on branch `task/<key>` in lower case

activeLink.description: The chat or orchestration task working on it right now, filled in when read: what makes a card live. Null when nothing is.

bounces.description: Times the verifying role sent it back to `in_progress` in the current round of work, compared with  {@link  ProjectFlowSettings.maxBounces } ; a person moving it starts a new round. Written by the flow by column: absent reads as 0.

waiting.description: What it waits for from the person, which the board shows in the idle colour with a word. Written by the flow by column: absent reads as null, waiting for nothing.

pullRequest.description: Its newest pull request; absent or null when it never had one

closedAt.description: When it last entered `done`; null while it is anywhere else

WorkItemPriority.description: Not a status: only `urgent` may be shown in a colour.

WorkItemAssignee.description: Who a work item is assigned to: the person, or a team role once the Team module exists. A discriminated union, so a kind added later (a named member) leaves the existing ones as they are.

WorkItemRef.description: Another work item as a field refers to it: enough to draw its chip without fetching it.

checkedBy.description: Who checked it; null while unchecked

AcceptanceCriterion.description: One entry of the acceptance checklist, checked on its own. Its position is its order in the list.

WorkItemRelationType.description: `blocks` and `blocked_by` only. Stored once, as `blocks`, and reported from both ends: the item that blocks shows `blocks`, the other `blocked_by`. Orchestrating a selection turns them into the graph's `dependsOn`.

chatId.description: The chat's session id; for an orchestration task, the chat of its worker once it has one

documentKind.description: For a `document` link, what kind of document it is; absent or null for the others

teamRole.description: The team role whose flow run made the link (the Product Owner's specification, QA's chat); absent or null for a link a person or a chat outside the flow made

name.description: The chat's title or the task's name, filled in when read; null when it is gone

chatState.description: Filled in when read, for a chat

taskStatus.description: Filled in when read, for an orchestration task

WorkItemLink.description: A chat, an orchestration task or a document tied to a work item. An item keeps every link, not only the last.

WorkItemLinkKind.description: What a work item can be linked to: what can act on it ( {@link  WorkItemSourceKind } ), and a document of the project (a specification, an architecture decision) tied to it by the Documents module.

WorkItemLinkRole.description:
The part a linked chat, orchestration task or document played in the item's life. The roles past `origin` follow the fixed columns, so they cannot grow with the flow: whichever team role a project puts on a column, its chat is `refine` in `backlog` and `todo`, `work` in `in_progress` and `verify` in `in_review`.

- `origin`: the item was created from it (the chat of "Create a task from this message", or a   document the assistant proposed items from).
- `refine`: refined it before work started; for a document, the specification refinement wrote.
- `work`: worked on it ("Work on it", a node of an orchestration built from it); for a document,   one written while working, such as an architecture decision.
- `verify`: verified it against its acceptance criteria; for a document, the verification report.
- `reference`: tied to it by hand, without playing a part in its life. Documents only, in practice.

`refine`, `work` and `verify` are also what a flow run's chat gets, by its  {@link  FlowStage } ; a client handles every member all the same.

DocumentKind.description: What a document tied to a work item is: `spec`, a specification (the Product Owner's, refining); `adr`, an architecture decision; `report`, a verification report (QA's); `doc`, anything else.

WorkItemWaitReason.description: Why an item waits for the person under the flow by column: `approval`, an agent finished and asks for the move to `done`, which only a person makes; `bounces`, verification sent it back more times than the project allows; `merge`, the person approved it and its pull request is open on GitHub, waiting for the person to merge it there. Each ends when a person moves it; `merge` also ends when the PR is merged (the item reaches `done`) or closed unmerged (back to `approval`).

host.description: The host that holds it; absent reads as `github` (rows opened before hosts existed)

number.description: Null until the host's CLI answered the create

ref.description: How the host writes the number: `#12` or `!12`; null without a number

base.description: The default branch it is proposed to

ci.description: Null until the watcher first read it

conflicts.description: The paths the update left conflicted, while `phase` is `conflict` or `awaiting-verify`

error.description: Why the last attempt failed: a step or readiness code, and git's or gh's first line of error

checkedAt.description: When the watcher last asked gh about it

WorkItemPullRequest.description: An item's pull request, the newest of its rows: an item keeps every PR it had, closed ones too.

id.description: Ours and stable: the key changes with the prefix, the id never does

description.description: Markdown. worktree.description: The item's own git worktree, once something worked on it, on branch `task/<key>` in lower case

activeLink.description: The chat or orchestration task working on it right now, filled in when read: what makes a card live. Null when nothing is.

bounces.description: Times the verifying role sent it back to `in_progress` in the current round of work, compared with  {@link  ProjectFlowSettings.maxBounces } ; a person moving it starts a new round. Written by the flow by column: absent reads as 0.

waiting.description: What it waits for from the person, which the board shows in the idle colour with a word. Written by the flow by column: absent reads as null, waiting for nothing.

pullRequest.description: Its newest pull request; absent or null when it never had one

closedAt.description: When it last entered `done`; null while it is anywhere else

children.description: For an epic, the items it groups

pullRequestReadiness.description: Whether approving it opens a pull request; absent or null for an item of a project that is not imported

WorkItemDetail.description: One work item with what its page shows beyond the card: `GET /work-items/:itemId`, or `GET /work-items/by-key/:key` for its key (`AGN-12`, in any case; 404 when no project's item has it, since a key prefix is unique among projects).

source.description: The chat or orchestration task an agent wrote it from; null for the person

WorkItemComment.description: Written by the person or by an agent; Markdown, no attachments.

from.description: Null when there was nothing before: `created`, a criterion or a relation added

to.description: Null when there is nothing after: a criterion or a relation removed

cause.description: Set when a chat or an orchestration made the change, rather than someone acting on the item

WorkItemHistoryEntry.description: One change to one field. Written by the service, never by the caller: an update that changes three fields writes three entries.

WorkItemHistoryValue.description: A plain value for a scalar field, the list for `labels`, and a snapshot for everything else.

host.description: The host that holds it; absent reads as `github` (entries written before hosts existed)

ref.description: How the host writes the number: `#12` or `!12`; null without a number

WorkItemHistoryPullRequest.description: A pull request as a history entry records it: opened, conflicted, merged or closed.

WorkItemHistoryRef.description: A referenced thing (an epic, a milestone, a link) as it was when the entry was written, so the history still reads after it is renamed or deleted. For a work item, `key` is composed when read, like every key.

WorkItemHistoryCriterion.description: A criterion as a history entry records it.

detail.description: The raw line git or the CLI answered with, shown in mono beside the worded reason; null when ready

defaultBranch.description: The default branch, when it could be found

host.description: The code host the remote belongs to; null when none could be told

hostname.description: The remote's host name, without user, secret or port; null when there is none

remedy.description: The one thing to do about a not-ready status; null when ready or when nothing can be done

PullRequestReadiness.description: Whether approving an item of this project opens its pull request. Computed from git and the host's CLI and cached for 60 s, so a board read never waits on an auth probe.

PullRequestNotReadyReason.description: Why a project cannot open pull requests (or merge requests); `ready` when it can. "Pull request" in these types means a PR or an MR: the host decides the word.

PullRequestRemedy.description: What a person can do about a not-ready project: a link to follow, never a command to copy.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Replaces the whole checklist, in this order

afterId.description: The item it goes right after in the target column; null puts it first, absent puts it last

MoveWorkItemRequest.description: Moves an item to a column and a place in it. The place is named by a neighbour rather than an index, so two people reordering at once do not land items on top of each other.

MoveWorkItemResult.description: A move always succeeds; going over the column's limit is reported, never refused.

limit.description: Null when the column has no limit

count.description: Every item in the column but its epics, whatever the filter: an epic takes no place under the limit

documentPath.description: For a `document` link: the document's path, relative to the project

CreateWorkItemLinkRequest.description: Every kind and role is accepted by the contract. A document is tied by hand through `POST /work-items/:itemId/documents` ( {@link  TieDocumentRequest } ), with the role `reference`.

closedAt.description: When it was last closed; null while open

Milestone.description: A named goal (`v0.19`) with no date: open or closed, and how far its work items are.

MilestoneProgress.description: Derived from the milestone's work items, epics left out: they group work, they are not work.

projectId.description: Null for the All projects board, whose columns carry no limit

columns.description: Always the five columns, in  {@link  WorkItemStatus }  order

pullRequestReadiness.description: A project's board: whether approving opens a pull request. Absent on the All projects board

checkout.description: A project's board: its checkout against the default branch; null when the project is not ready

limit.description: Null when the column has no limit

count.description: Every item in the column but its epics, whatever the filter: an epic takes no place under the limit

total.description: Every item that passes the filter, across the pages

nextCursor.description: Opaque: pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last

labels.description: Items carrying any of these labels

q.description: Searched in the title and the description, and matched against the key

cursor.description: `nextCursor` of the previous page; absent for the first

WorkItemPageQuery.description: `GET /projects/:id/work-items/page` and `GET /work-items/page` (All projects): the list a page at a time, in the same order as the whole list, with the same filter. `GET /projects/:id/work-items` and `GET /work-items` still answer the whole list as an array.

doneLimit.description: Items of the Done column to hold; default `BOARD_DONE_PAGE`, at most `WORK_ITEMS_PAGE_MAX`

BoardQuery.description: `GET /projects/:id/work-items/board` and `GET /work-items/board` take the filter ( {@link  WorkItemFilter } ) and this. The Done column grows without end, so it is paged: a board holds its newest closed items, and "and N more" asks again with the next multiple of the page. Asking for a larger limit rather than a cursor keeps one board per query, which the event feed refreshes whole.

WorkOnWorkItemRequest.description: What a chat started on a work item may be given. The prompt is built from the item (its title, description and acceptance criteria) and the directory is its worktree, so neither is taken here.

provider.description: The provider to run on; the first one in the person's order that can run chats when absent

toolPreset.description: Id of a stored  {@link  ToolPreset } ; an explicit `allowedTools` wins over it. A new chat that names neither this nor `allowedTools` takes the default preset; `null` opts out of it (and, on a resume or a fork, drops the preset the chat had).

mcp.description: MCP servers this chat starts with; absent keeps what it has, `null` goes back to what the CLI loads on its own

maxBudgetUsd.description: Ceiling on what this execution may spend

permissionPrompts.description: `host` sends permissions, questions and plans to the panel; `none`, the default, denies them

account.description: Pin it to a claude-swap account (slot number, email or alias) instead of the active one; `null` unpins a chat on a resume or a fork. A pinned chat that hits its limit is unpinned by the rotation.

ChatStartOptions.description: What can be chosen when a process starts on a chat, whether it is new, resumed or a fork.

item.description: The item as it is once the chat started: in its worktree, and in `in_progress` unless a person had it elsewhere

OrchestrateWorkItemsRequest.description: A selection of work items of one project to orchestrate, in the order they were picked.

duplicate.description: An open item already seems to cover the draft; the warning does not name which

externalBlockers.description: Items outside the selection, not done yet, that block an item of it: the graph cannot wait for them

WorkItemOrchestrationDraft.description: A graph to review, not a launched one: one node per item, each naming its item in `workItemId`, and `dependsOn` from the `blocks` relations inside the selection. `POST /orchestrations` launches it.

text.description: The message, which becomes the description

title.description: Default: the message's first line

CreateWorkItemFromMessageRequest.description: Creates a work item in `backlog` from a message of a chat, linked to that chat.

summary.description: Null while nothing has worked on it in a worktree, or once its branch is gone

WorkItemChanges.description: What the item's own branch changed, read from git the way a chat's worktree is.

WorkItemPullRequestResult.description: The answer of `POST /work-items/:itemId/pull-request`: 202 while it is prepared, 200 when one was open already.

enabled.description: The Team module is on; with it off the members are still served, and the client hides them

unassignedAgents.description: Agent files in the project's `.claude/agents/` that no member uses, which "add a member" offers

model.description: Model alias or id of the agent that plays it (`opus`, `sonnet`)

responsibility.description: One line on what it answers for

agent.description: Name of the agent file in the project's `.claude/agents/`, without `.md`

writes.description: Paths or globs, relative to the project, the member may write; absent means no restriction of Agentry's own. Enforced on the chats Agentry starts for it through the CLI's permission rules; from a terminal it is only what the agent file says.

commands.description: The shell commands the member may run in the flow's work stage, as patterns the CLI's permission rules take (`npm test`, `pnpm *`: each becomes `Bash(<pattern>)`). Absent means `Bash` is not restricted there, as before; present means only these, and an empty list means no shell at all. The refine and verify stages keep their own tool sets. Checked with  {@link  isTeamCommandPattern  } .

columns.description: The columns it answers for under the flow, in board order; empty for a role that is only consulted

running.description: Its flow runs working now, oldest first; empty when it is idle

lastRun.description: Its latest run that ended, for "refined AGN-47 1 h ago"; null when it never ran

TeamMember.description: A member as `GET /projects/:id/team` serves it: the metadata, its file, and what it is doing.

description.description: As the file's frontmatter says them; null when the file is missing or leaves them out

TeamAgentFileState.description: The member's agent file as it is on disk: `ok`, it matches the metadata; `missing`, it was deleted (the member still shows, and its file can be written again); `drifted`, its frontmatter says something the metadata does not ( {@link  TeamAgentFile.drift } ). A drifted or hand-edited file is reported, never overwritten.

TeamAgentDriftField.description: A frontmatter field of the agent file that disagrees with the member's metadata.

item.description: Filled in when read; null once the item is gone

agent.description: The member's agent file name, as `claude --agent` takes it

step.description: The stage as the person reads it, by its column: `check` is a `refine` in `todo`

column.description: The column the card entered that started it

chatId.description: The chat it runs in; null while queued. A Developer's run continues the item's work chat when there is one

activity.description: What the chat is doing now, filled in when read while it runs

summary.description: The result's summary, once it ended with one

error.description: Why it failed or was cancelled, in English, as the core or the CLI said it; null otherwise

cause.description: Why it failed or was cancelled, as a code to word; null otherwise, and on an old run whose error reads as none

retryOf.description: The failed run a person retried with this one (`POST /flow-runs/:runId/retry`); null for a run a card entering its column started

queuedBy.description: Who queued it when it was not a card entering its column: `person` for a run a person started from the Flow screen's "start the waiting cards" (`POST /projects/:id/flow/start-waiting`). Null for a run a card's entry queued, and for a retry, which `retryOf` names.

retriedBy.description: On a run that did not pass, the next run of the same step on the item, whatever started it (a retry or the card entering the column again): what the person's retry, or the flow, did next. Null until there is one.

retryable.description: Whether `POST /flow-runs/:runId/retry` would queue it again now: it failed, nothing has run that step on the item since, the item is still in the run's column, and the flow is on with a member answering for the column.

restarts.description: Times a restart cut it off and it went on in its chat; past `MAX_FLOW_RESTARTS` it fails

continuations.description: Times the flow sent it back to its chat because its turn ended with work still owed (no structured result, uncommitted changes, or a last message that offers, asks or announces instead of doing): at most `MAX_CONTINUATIONS`, after which the result it has is judged as it is

language.description: The person's language, which the first line of its chat's prompt (`<Role> · <KEY>`, the title the chat is listed by) is written in, kept so a restart words it the same. Absent on a run stored before it was kept, which reads as `en`.

FlowRun.description: One run of a team member on a work item, queued, running or ended. Rows, so it survives a restart.

FlowRunState.description: `queued` waits for a place under `maxParallel`; `running` has its chat; `ended` has an outcome.

FlowRunRef.description: Another run as a run refers to it: enough to say what it did and open its chat.

AgentryLanguage.description: The languages Agentry speaks. TeamFromTemplateRequest.description:

`POST /projects/:id/team/from-template` answers the whole  {@link  Team } : with 201 when it added at least one member, and with 200 when nothing changed (every role was already on the team), like the other creating routes. Sending it twice is harmless either way.

model.description: Model alias or id of the agent that plays it (`opus`, `sonnet`)

responsibility.description: One line on what it answers for

commands.description: Absent or null leaves the shell unrestricted in the work stage ( {@link  ProjectTeamMember.commands } )

createFile.description: Write a starting agent file for the role when there is none; an existing file is never overwritten

PutTeamMemberRequest.description: Creates or replaces a member's metadata (`PUT /projects/:id/team/:agent`). The agent file itself is edited through `/config/resources/agents/:name?project=`.

queued.description: In the order they will start

ProjectFlow.description: `GET /projects/:id/flow`: what the flow is doing in a project now.

total.description: Every run that passes the filter, across the pages

nextCursor.description: Opaque: pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last

FlowRunPage.description: A page of a project's flow runs, newest first.

total.description: 0 while the flow, the Team module or the Board module is off

columns.description: In board order; only the columns with at least one waiting card

FlowWaiting.description: `GET /projects/:id/flow/waiting`: the cards a flow switched on would not start by itself. role.description: The team role that answers for the column, matching  {@link  ProjectTeamRole.role }

FlowWaitingColumn.description: One column of  {@link  FlowWaiting } : how many of its cards wait, and the role that answers for it.

queued.description: Runs queued, one per waiting card

startingNow.description: Of those, how many the project's `maxParallel` lets start now: `min(queued, maxParallel − running)`

waiting.description: `queued − startingNow`: they start as places come free

FlowStartWaitingResult.description: `POST /projects/:id/flow/start-waiting`: what queuing the waiting cards did.

criteria.description: Verification only: every acceptance criterion of the item, each judged on its own

FlowRunResult.description: The structured result every flow run ends with, through the CLI's `--json-schema`. `summary` becomes the member's comment on the item; `verdict` is QA's only.

id.description: The criterion's id, as the run's prompt lists it

note.description: What was checked, or what is missing

needsPerson.description: No flow run can check it: it needs a push, a pull request, a tool or service the run does not have, or a person's eyes. It is left unchecked for the person who approves the item and does not reject the run (refines decision 18).

reason.description: Why the team should remember it

FlowMemoryProposal.description: A memory entry a flow run proposes, as its result carries it.

path.description: Relative to the project, inside the documents folder (`docs/specs/agn-28-board.md`)

FlowRunDocument.description: A document a flow run wrote in the item's worktree, reported so Agentry ties it to the item.

handed.description: What a flow run is handed: the newest entries that fit the cap

nextBefore.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; null on the last

text.description: Markdown; for `closed`, the item's title as it was

item.description: Filled in when read; null when there is no item or it is gone

author.description: Who wrote or proposed it: the person, or the agent and its role

approvedBy.description: Who approved it: the move to `done` for `closed`, the proposal for `memory`; null for what a person wrote

documentPath.description: A document it refers to (an architecture decision), relative to the project

sources.description: For `closed`: the chats and orchestration tasks that worked on the item

CreateJournalEntryRequest.description: An entry written by hand. `closed` and `memory` are Agentry's to write.

journalEntryId.description: The journal entry an approval to the journal wrote

tiedCount.description: Files tied to at least one item

ProjectDocuments.description: `GET /projects/:id/documents`: the tree of the documents folder.

children.description: For a directory, its entries, directories first; absent for a file

fileCount.description: For a directory, the Markdown files under it at any depth

title.description: For a file: its first `# ` heading, when it has one

baseUpdatedAt.description: The `updatedAt` the editor started from; when the file changed since (an agent wrote it), the write is refused with 409 instead of overwriting it. Absent writes whatever is there.

names.description: A few names a client may list beside it: the open milestones (`v0.20`), the files of a group

responsibility.description: One line on what it answers for

saved.description: Where it was saved, once accepted: its scope and its path there; null otherwise

content.description: What it has written of the whole file so far, frontmatter included; empty before the first part

AssistantResourceDraft.description: The resource a running "Create with AI" has written so far; nothing of it is saved.

description.description: For a `resources` run, the one resource to build ("Create with AI"), with `resourceKind`; for a `project` or `work-items` run, what the project is for when there is nothing to read

focus.description: For a `work-items` run ("Suggest tasks"), what to look for ("the checkout's error handling"): the prompt words it as the area to propose work in, not as what the project is for. Refused on the other kinds. The language is not a field: it is the request's `Accept-Language`.

supersede.description: Mark the pending proposals of the latest finished run of this kind `superseded`. Default false

StartAssistantRunRequest.description: `POST /projects/:id/assistant/runs`. One run at a time per project and kind: a second one while one runs is refused with 409. A new run leaves the previous one's pending proposals as they are, unless `supersede` says to set them aside ("Suggest again").

agent.description: Name of the agent file it would write in `.claude/agents/`, without `.md`

writes.description: Paths or globs it may write; empty means nothing but work items ("writes: nothing, only tasks")

instructions.description: The agent file's body; empty lets the team service write its starting one

resource.description: The editor's save: the name, content and scope the person left

epicId.description: An existing epic of the project it belongs to

allowedHosts.description: Host names this wrapper answers to besides loopback, each a name or a `*.domain` pattern with at least two labels below the wildcard. Only the configured part: the exact names a running tunnel adds for itself are not listed here, because nobody may edit them.

maxConcurrentRuns.description: How many runs may work at once; a change applies to the next run, without a restart

defaultPermissionMode.description: The `--permission-mode` of a run that does not ask for one; applies to the next run

providersStepSeen.description: The first-run Providers step was shown and answered (continued or skipped). Kept here rather than in the browser so a second browser, a phone or the desktop app does not ask again; the step still returns whenever no provider is ready.

UpdateAppSettingsRequest.description: `PUT /settings/app`: the settings to change, and only those. A setting the environment set is refused rather than written to the file, where it would do nothing until the variable goes away and then change behaviour by surprise.

startWithAgentry.description: Open the tunnel whenever Agentry starts; off unless the person turns it on

UpdateTunnelSettingsRequest.description: `PUT /tunnel/settings`: the settings to change, and only those.

propertyNames.description: An agent provider, by the id its manifest declares (`claude-code`, `codex`, …). A string and not a closed union, so adding a provider is adding a folder in core and never a change here.

order.description: Provider ids in the order the UI lists them

defaultProvider.description: The provider a new chat starts with; null takes the first ready one in `order`

ProvidersSettings.description: `providers.json` in the data directory: which providers are on, in what order they are offered, which one new work starts with, and where a binary lives when the search cannot find it.

binaryPath.description: Absolute path of the binary to use instead of searching for one; null searches

ProviderSettingsEntry.description: What a person chose for one provider.

CodeHostsSettings.description: `hosts.json` in the data directory. A disabled host's projects read `unsupported-host`.

binaryPath.description: Absolute path of the binary to use instead of searching for one; null searches

CodeHostSettingsEntry.description: What a person chose for one code host.

ProjectCodeHost.description: `GET /projects/:id/code-host`: the readiness and the parsed remote.

ProjectCodeHostRemote.description: A project's remote as Agentry parsed it: never the URL, which can carry a user and a secret.

OrchestrationPullRequestAnswer.description: The answer of `POST /orchestrations/:id/pull-request`; the first three fields are what it always had.

jev.description: The key itself is never returned, only whether one is saved and its last four characters

mode.description: Absent reads as `off` for every point

threshold.description: Act points only, 0.5..0.99; absent reads as the point's default

key.description: The Jev key; saved with mode 0600 and never returned

notice.description: The general privacy notice (D12): what leaves the machine when a point runs on Jev

savesRun.description: True when acting on it avoids a Claude run (feeds "Claude runs saved")

stateVersion.description: Bumps when the shape of the state changes, which clears the consent given for an older one

effective.description: Mode, threshold and consent after project, then global, then the point's defaults

DecisionPointKind.description: A suggest point prepares something a person decides; an act point changes what happens next

DecisionScope.description: `global`: settings only global; `project`: a project may override them

DecisionPrimitive.description: The three typed questions, named as Jev names them: a choice, a score on a rubric, a yes/no.

source.description: `last` is what the latest request sent; `built` is built locally now and not sent

state.description: The exact state that was sent

threshold.description: The threshold in force, act points only

paletteAction.description: What the palette's person did with the proposal; null until they ran or dismissed

DecisionSubjectKind.description: What a decision was about; the `subject_kind` column of the history

options.description: 2..255 options; ids are stable, labels are what the provider reads

DecisionChoiceQuestion.description: Questions and rubrics are English (D4): providers read `label` and `description`, never a translation

levels.description: A rubric of 2..10 levels, lowest first

summary.description: What happened, in words the History row shows; the point's resolver writes it

agreed.description: True when the answer matched what happened; the person's feedback overrides the inference

detail.description: Point-specific facts (a status, a count), for the row's detail

commandId.description: The command that ran; null when the palette closed without one

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null at the end

subjectKind.description: What the decision was about: the mark reads the rows of one subject

visible.description: Only rows that changed something a person sees

meanConfidence.description: Mean confidence of the rows that have one; null when none do
